The end of a level. Clears the player's claimed total and draws the timer bar. In practice: the level-over message and back to the title (reload_alien). Otherwise: the next tune is chosen, the messages are drawn (level_messages, the split or bonus summary at $17A7), the music player is copied back to $E000 and its own interrupt installed ($1688), and the tune plays until fire is pressed or it ends (with the extra message at $1786 if it lasts). Then the sound stops, zero page and page 2 are saved at $6000/$6100 (the load below clears them), TAITO is loaded from the disk (load_taito), and the next level begins (next_level at $1F96).

Part of title_bitmap2, 768 bytes in; referred to here by burst_frame, burst_replay.
Title bitmap rows 6-8 ($6800-$6BFF).
Part of title_bitmap3, 256 bytes in; referred to here by burst_frame, burst_replay.
Part of title_bitmap3, 512 bytes in; referred to here by burst_frame, burst_replay.
Part of title_bitmap3, 768 bytes in; referred to here by burst_frame, burst_replay.
Title bitmap rows 9-11 ($6C00-$6FFF).
Title bitmap rows 11-14 ($7000-$73FF).
Title bitmap rows 14-17 ($7400-$77FF).
Title bitmap rows 17-20 ($7800-$7BFF).
Title bitmap rows 20-24 ($7C00-$7F3F).

The game's entry, where the crack's loader jumps once ALIEN is in (JMP $8000 with $01 = $36). Points the NMI at the RTI at $1180 (RESTORE does nothing), sets the stack, banks BASIC and the KERNAL out ($01 = $35), keeps the boot drive number (8 or 9, else 8) at $1550 and the KERNAL's PAL flag $02A6 at $1551, and patches the music player's tempo at $410D/$410E (in the copy source at $4000) with $06A9 on NTSC or $05F0 on PAL. Then it builds the title (title_screen_setup, show_title_picture), picks a tune, and falls into title_loop.

Title loop: start tune X (music_init at $E000), set music_playing, enable interrupts, then wait. Fire (bit 4 of joy_title) goes to the menu at menu_start; the tune ending (music_playing cleared by the interrupt) or about four frames of no input in wait_frames_or_input lets the attract sequence run: music_stop, attract_demo at $C000, then the title is rebuilt with a new tune and the loop starts again.

The menu: rebuilds the screen as the option list (menu_draw at $C830), selection 0, and moves the highlight bar with the stick: down (bit 1) steps menu_choice forward, up (bit 0) back, wrapping 0..2. The bar is a raster split (menu_raster_* at $8255): menu_highlight writes the band's top and bottom lines ($7F/$95, $A7/$BD or $CF/$E5) in the vertical blank. Fire starts the chosen game at menu_fire; letting the tune end returns to the title.
The low byte of the STA $8259 at $80A8 in menu_start. The BIT $80A9 at $99AA in draw_step only skips the next instruction (its operand is the LDA #$80 that follows) and does not read this byte.
Menu idle path: three waits with no input, then pick the next tune and restart it; music_playing is set again.

Fire on the menu: menu_choice 0 = one player (practice_flag 0, two_player_flag 0), 1 = two players (two_player_flag $80), 2 = practice (practice_flag $80). Stops the music, clears the play bitmap at $2000 and the shadow page set at $C000 with fill_pages, sets current_player to '1', and jumps to game_start.
An RTI nothing reaches.
Reads the RUN/STOP key on its own: CIA1 port A drives row 7 only and port B is read until two reads agree; returns A = 0 (Z set) while RUN/STOP is held. Interrupt flag preserved.
Called every frame from the play interrupt. RUN/STOP pauses the game: silence the SID (sound_off), wait for RUN/STOP to be let go, then wait for any stick movement or fire on either port, and resume.
Waits up to 256 frames for joy_title to become non-zero. Returns carry set if the stick or fire was used, clear if it timed out.

Title and menu interrupt, first of a chain of three raster interrupts. Plays one frame of the music (music_play at $E006, which returns the still-playing flag, kept in music_playing), samples both joystick ports into joy_title, then points the IRQ vector at irq_menu_band_top and sets the next raster line from menu_band_top. Writes 0 to $D030 so a C128 stays at 1 MHz.

The menu highlight bar: the background colour outside the band ($8255), the band's colour ($8256), and the raster lines where the band starts ($8257) and ends ($8258). The menu sets them to colour 10 (light red) and the line pair of the chosen option.
Part of menu_raster_vars, 1 bytes in, read and written here by irq_menu_band_top, menu_draw, menu_start, title_screen_setup.
Part of menu_raster_vars, 2 bytes in; referred to here by irq_title_top, menu_draw, menu_start, title_screen_setup.
Part of menu_raster_vars, 3 bytes in; referred to here by irq_menu_band_top, menu_draw, menu_start, title_screen_setup.
Part of menu_raster_vars, 4 bytes in; referred to here by menu_fire, menu_start.
Second title interrupt: at the band's top line, waits for the next line, sets the background to the band colour, and arms irq_menu_band_bottom for the band's last line.
Third title interrupt: at the band's last line, restores the normal background colour and re-arms irq_title_top at line 251.
Takes the next tune number from the shuffled list at tune_order ($16BD), counting tune_index ($16C7) down; when the list is used up, shuffle_tunes builds a new order. Returns the tune in A.

Draws one character into the bitmap at ($02) by XOR: A is the character's code ($20 clears the cell instead). The glyph comes from the font at $BD00, eight bytes per character from '(' ($28); each pixel pair that has either bit set is widened to both bits, so the hires glyph shows as solid multicolour pixels of colour 3.
Advances the inline-argument pointer at $06/$07 and returns the byte there.

Prints the text that follows the JSR into the bitmap and returns past it. The arguments are groups of: bitmap address (low, high), the characters, a 0; a further 0 ends the list. Each character is drawn by xor_glyph, eight bytes (one cell) to the right of the last.

The play interrupt, once a frame at raster line 252 (bit 7 of $D011 cleared, $D012 = $FC). Banks the I/O in, checks for pause (pause_check), runs the sound effects (sfx_update at $B803), counts down sfx_lock, and unless play_frozen ($15C8 bit 7) is set reads the stick (read_stick) and animates the enemy sprites (sprite_anim), then counts down frame_tick ($B2), which paces the main loop, and the animation timer $5D.

Reads the joystick into stick ($2E): both ports EORed together, so a stick in either port works, bits 0-3 the directions and bit 4 fire, set when pressed. A diagonal (up or down with left or right) keeps fire but takes the last straight direction, kept at last_dir ($840C), so the marker never moves diagonally.
last_dir: the last straight stick direction, kept by read_stick so that a diagonal keeps the marker moving the way it was going.

Installs the play interrupt: interrupts off, $01 = $35, $00 = $2F, black border and background, clears zero page from $04 and page 2, gives CIA1's ports back to the keyboard, points $FFFE and $0314 at irq_play, turns CIA1's timer interrupts off, and enables the raster interrupt at line 252.

Clears the shadow maps at $6000 and $E000 and, unless keep_bitmap ($1558) is set, the bitmap at $2000 (else restores it with restore_bitmap), draws the field border (draw_border), sets the fill patterns $4F/$50 to $55/$AA, then sets the screen colours (set_play_colours) and reinstalls the play interrupt.
The work of clear_play_memory before the border: clears the $6000 and $E000 planes and the bitmap (or restores it), draws the border and sets the fill patterns.
Copies 8 KB from $2000-$3FFF to $C000-$DFFF with the I/O banked out ($01 = $34), from the top down: the play screen saved under the I/O area, where restore_bitmap ($88B8) finds it.
Draws the field's rectangle twice: once with all three pattern bytes $4F-$51 at $FF: draw_rect, then draw_rect_outer one pixel outside it.

Draws the field's border: the rectangle from field_left/right/top/bottom ($1575-$1578) with all three pattern bytes $4F-$51 at $FF, then the rectangle one pixel outside it with $FF, $55 and $00. Both use the plotting line routine (line_begin_all at $AA45 and line_all_to at $AACE).
Draws the rectangle with corners field_left,field_top and field_right,field_bottom as four lines (line_begin_all, line_all_to).
Draws the rectangle one pixel outside draw_rect's on every side, with the same line routines.

Draws the Sparx timer bar at full length unless timer_stopped ($91D8 bit 7): 24 cells down the bitmap column at $2258, the left half of each byte set to pattern %0101 (colour from the screen matrix's high nibble). Then timer_bar_reset sets its two ends.

Sets the timer bar's two ends: the top end pointer $06/$07 = $2258 with row index $A1 = 1, the bottom end pointer $08/$09 = $3F18 with row index $A2 = 7, the next end to shorten $A3 = $80, and the countdown $A4 = 96 frames.

Counts timer_delay ($A4) down; at zero, reloads it (3 in practice or with bit 6 of $6C set, 5 with bit 7 of $6C set, otherwise 7) and takes one pixel row off the bar, alternately from the top (timer_bar_eat_top) and the bottom (timer_bar_eat_bottom).
Clears the bar's top row: the left half of the byte at ($06),$A1 is wiped, moving down a cell (+320 bytes) every eight rows. When the byte is already empty the two ends have met: timer_bar_empty.
Clears the bar's bottom row, moving up a cell every eight rows; an empty byte means the ends have met (timer_bar_empty).

The Sparx timer has run out: counts it in timer_runs ($0A). Outside practice, once timer_runs reaches the level's limit ($91D9) the timer stops for good (timer_stopped = $80); otherwise the bar is redrawn full. When timer_runs equals $91D6 and bit 7 of $159B is set, the pair at $B587/$B588 is copied into $92/$93 and $94/$95, sfx_lock is set to 255 and sound effect 5 starts.

Converts a 24-bit number (A low, X middle, Y high) to decimal digits at digits_out ($874C), most significant first, by repeated subtraction of the powers of ten in the table at pow10 ($8728); leading zeros are skipped (except the last), and the list ends with a 0.
Stores digit A in digits_out and ends the list with 0.
Working copy of the number score_to_digits is converting (three bytes) and its flag and output index.
Part of bcd_work, 1 bytes in, read and written here by score_to_digits.
Part of bcd_work, 2 bytes in; referred to here by score_to_digits.
Part of bcd_work, 3 bytes in; referred to here by score_to_digits.
Part of bcd_work, 4 bytes in; referred to here by digit_store, score_to_digits.
Powers of ten as four-byte little-endian numbers, from 1 to 100,000,000, read by score_to_digits from the top.
The decimal digits of the last number converted by score_to_digits, as ASCII-coded digits for the font, ended by 0.
Draws character A at the bitmap address in $02/$03 by copying its eight font bytes from $BD00 (a space clears the cell). Unlike xor_glyph it overwrites.
Copies the font bytes from $BD00 into the bitmap at $23A0 (32 bytes) and $24E0 (32 bytes): the four-cell QIX logo in the panel to the right of the field.
Sixteen-byte glyph copier (A minus 4 times 16 from $BEC0 into ($02)); nothing calls it.

Silences everything: fades the SID volume from 10 to 0 over about forty frames (unless sound_off_done is already set), clears the SID registers, stops the music (music_stop at $B800) and the sound effects (play_sfx 0), and sets sound_off_done.
Entry of sound_off with A = 4 (the BIT skip): the same fade in fewer steps.
The operand of the LDX at $87E3: the frames per volume step in sound_off's fade, set to 8 or 4 by its two entries.
Set to 0 by sound_off; compared with by $94E6.
Frames during which a new sound effect cannot interrupt the current one; counted down by the play interrupt.
Starts sound effect A unless sfx_lock is running and A is not one of the effects 0, 1, 2, 5 or 9 that may always interrupt.
Tail of play_sfx: hands the effect number in A to the sound-effect starter at $B806.
Bit 7 set once sound_off has faded and silenced the SID; play_sfx clears it when it starts effect 0, 1, 2, 5 or 9, and the menu and the game's end clear it.
Copies the 8,000-byte plane at $2000 to $E000 (copy_plane).
Copies the 8,000-byte plane at $E000 to $C000 (copy_plane).
Copies the 8,000-byte plane at $C000 to $6000 (copy_plane).

Copies the 8,000 bytes at $4000-$5F3F to $E000-$FF3F (copy_plane): puts the music player and its tunes where they run, at $E000. The start-up does it once; the end of a level does it again, because play uses $E000 as a work plane.
Copies $1F40 bytes (one bitmap's worth) from page X to page Y, with the I/O and both ROMs banked out ($01 = $34) so that RAM under $D000 can be read and written; $01 is restored afterwards.
The two masks merge_column uses: $F0 keeps the left pair of multicolour pixels, $0F the right.

Copies one half of each byte (nibble_masks,X) from the plane at ($08) into the bitmap at ($06), leaving the other half alone, down 25 cells (entry $8883) or 24 cells (entry $8886, A = $18 with the BIT skip), one byte per cell, 320 bytes apart.
merge_column for 24 cells (A = $18).
Column offset used by redraw_panel_edges.

Clears the plane at $6000 and draws the border there (draw_border_solid), then merges the two-cell strips at $2140 and $2240 of the bitmap with the same strips of the $6000 plane, column by column (merge_column): it puts back the border's edges after the bitmap was restored.
The column loop of redraw_panel_edges, also called alone by switch_player after the board is restored: merges the two-cell strips at $2140 and $2240 from the $6000 plane into the bitmap.

Sets up a new life or round: copies $1569 to $33, clears the timer runs and timer_stopped, $A5/$A6, $1559/$155A, the claimed percentage ($020A) and $0203; puts the marker ($31,$32) and its last corner ($29,$2A) at the middle of the bottom edge (x = (field_right - field_left)/2, y = field_bottom); calls $AF82 with A = 1, $91DA and $9EA0, clears the play memory, sets up the Qix ($B530), takes a random value (random at $A58D) to pick $0205 from the table at $121B, and clears $028F/$0290, $154D and $0202.

Starts a game: blanks the screen ($D011 = 0), clears the play memory, saves the empty bitmap under the I/O ($84AD), runs $8F9E, installs the play interrupt, takes the starting lives from $1567 into lives ($026E), sets the level ($B7) to 1, clears both players' scores ($1560-$1562 and $1563-$1565) and $155C-$155F, sets $02B2/$02B3 to $80, sets the first round up (round_setup), sets multicolour ($D016 = $D8), the bitmap at $2000 ($D018 bit 3) and VIC bank 0 (bitmap mode itself is turned on by game_start), and sets each player's next extra-life score to 50,000 ($00C350 at $1F90-$1F92 and $1F93-$1F95).
From the menu: new_game, then the level loop (level_start).

Called once a pass from level_loop. If the marker has stopped while drawing ($5E bit 7) the Fuse appears and moves (fuse_step) every $5F passes, sound 10; past level 10 ($B7 >= 11) flag_8B0B is set. When the marker moves again ($5E clear) the Fuse is removed (fuse_off at $8AF6: sprite 1 off, sound 11).
Removes the Fuse: flag_8B0B cleared, sprite 1 turned off, sound 11.
Set to 2 by marker_check_edge (fire held, the marker on a line); while it is non-zero the main loop calls $991C once a pass instead of marker_step, counting it down.
Bit 7 set by $8AC4 once $B7 (the level) is 11 or more after $AFCE has run; cleared by $8AF6, which also turns sprite 1 off and plays sound 11.

One step of the marker from the main loop. Takes the stick ($2E), or while a line is being drawn ($9A bit 7) the direction already held ($9C); with no direction it returns. On the edge ($9A clear) the marker's position is kept as the last corner ($29,$2A and $ADEA/$ADEB). Then, with fire (bit 4 of the input) copied to $27 bit 7, it tries right, left, up and down in turn (marker_try_right/left/up/down), each only if that direction is pressed; a move onto a line flips the drawing flag $9A. Finally the position is written alternately to $0C/$0E and $0D/$0F for the line plotter.
The marker_step path when $2B bit 7 is clear: takes the stick ($2E) or the held direction ($9C) while drawing, the same as marker_step's tail.

Tries one pixel to the right: the candidate ($0206,$0207) is plotted with direction 8 ($AF82), then the pixels above and below the new position (in $12-$17) are tested in the $E000 plane against pattern_masks2 (test_pixel2); if either is set the move is checked against the drawn lines (marker_check_edge).
As marker_try_right, one pixel to the left (direction 4).
As marker_try_right, one pixel up (direction 1), testing the pixels to the left and right.
As marker_try_up, one pixel down (direction 2).

Decides whether the candidate position ($0206,$0207) is taken. A set pixel there in the $E000 plane that equals pixel_masks (colour 3) is taken at once (marker_move). A clear pixel is refused while $9A bit 7 is set, or when either side pixel ($12,$15 or $13,$16) is set; otherwise the pixel ahead ($14,$17) must be clear or colour 3, and then, if fire is held ($27 bit 7), $2B and $33 are set to $80 and count_8B08 to 2.
The direction being tried by marker_step: 8 right, 4 left, 1 up, 2 down.

Accepts the move: sets $11 bit 7, and places the marker sprite (sprite 0, pointer $21, hires, enabled) at the candidate position: x = (x + 7) * 2 with the ninth bit in $D010, y = y + 40. The position becomes the marker's ($31,$32).
Places the marker's sprite (sprite 0, pointer $21) at the candidate position ($0206,$0207) and makes it the marker's position ($31,$32).
Looks up the pixel at X,Y in the $E000 plane (pixel_addr) and compares it with pattern_masks2,X (the pixel in colour 2): Z set when equal.

Address of the pixel at x = X (0-159, multicolour pixels) and y = Y in the $E000 plane: row base from row_lo/row_hi ($123B/$1303) plus column offset from col_lo/col_hi ($13CB/$146B), ORed with $E000, into $55/$56. Returns the byte masked to that pixel (pixel_masks at $150B, by x AND 3), with X = x AND 3.
Called between the main loop's steps. If $1E bit 7 is set (the marker has been hit) it drops the caller's return and runs life_lost.

A life is lost: stops the fill (spawn reset $8AF6), redraws the timer bar, clears the slow-draw flag $154D, plays sound 9, blanks the sprites, then the death sequence: $8F24 (the line unwinds), $B2F4, $A774, marker back to the last corner (marker_reset), and sound_off. With no lives left ($026E) and not practice: the game-over message ($19EA), then, in a two-player game whose other player is still playing ($8DB6 clear), mark this one finished and switch players (switch_player); otherwise reload the game (reload_alien at $1B97). With lives left, a two-player game switches players before the next round.
Puts the marker back at its last corner ($29,$2A) and clears the timer runs, timer_stopped and the hit flag $1E, then redraws the panel (draw_status at $1CDE).
Bit 7 set when one player of a two-player game has lost all lives, so play no longer alternates.

After a pass of the main loop: if the marker was hit, check_death. If $28 bit 7 is set (a closed line is to be filled): $8AF6, sound 7 (or 8 when $23 bit 7 is set and $154D is clear), clear $70/$71 and area_lo/area_hi, and run $B243. Then, when $BB bit 7 and (after $B07C, $B0EC, $B0B4) $AB bit 7 are both set, increment $0291 and run $A1C0, $A23A and $A316 before ending the level; otherwise run the fill animation (claim_wait) and claim_check.
Runs the fill animation ($A90A) until it returns carry set, calling $ABAC between steps.

Scores the claimed area (score_fill), turns the claimed total into a percentage at claimed_pct ($020A), capped at 99, and compares it with the level's requirement ($B8). Below it: redraw the panel and, if a life was gained, sound the bell ($1A74), then go back to the main loop. At or above it: 1,000 points for every percent over the requirement (added to the score with add_bonus) and the level ends (level_end).
Low byte of the bonus being built by claim_check, 1,000 ($03E8) per percent over.

Scores a finished fill. The area counted by the fill ($70/$71, pixels) is halved, then doubled again unless the line was fast ($23 bit 7) with no forced slow scoring ($154D bit 7 clear): a slow line scores twice a fast one. Then for each split ($0291, the times this player has split the Qix so far in the game; only new_game clears it) the points are doubled again, but the doubling adds only the low byte to itself and carries into the high byte without doubling it: a bug, so from 256 points on each split adds less than the manual's doubling. The fill's area ($8EB7/$8EB8) is added to the current player's claimed total ($155C/$155D for player 1, $155E/$155F for player 2), and the points to the score (add_score).
Pixels claimed by the fill being scored, low byte; incremented by the fill routines.
Pixels claimed by the fill being scored, high byte.
Adds $70/$71 to the current player's 24-bit score ($1560-$1562 for player 1, $1563-$1565 for player 2) and returns the high byte of that player's claimed total.

The level is won: sound_off, timer bar redrawn, sprites off, the bonus ($028F/$0290) added to the score, the panel redrawn (with the extra-life bell if one was gained), then the end-of-level sequence at level_complete ($15D3).
Counter used by unwind_line.

The death animation: for $156B+1 steps, erases one segment from each end of the drawn line ($0228/$023C/$021E/$0232 for one end at index $B5, $0250/$0264/$0246/$025A for the other at $B6) with erase_segment ($98A5), stepping both indices down and wrapping them to $156B. The first byte of the bitmap is saved and restored around it.
Copies zero page ($02-$FF) to $5E02 and page 2 to $5F02: the first player's state, kept while the second plays.
Clears zero page from $02, page 2, and their saved copies at $5E00 and $5F00, and sets $01 = $35, $00 = $2F.

Two-player games: switches current_player between '1' and '2', saves this player's board (copy_2000_to_E000), redraws the panel edges and the player's name ($1A15), exchanges zero page and page 2 with the copies at $5E00/$5F00, restores the other player's board ($C000 to $6000, then rebuilds the visible bitmap from it with rebuild_bitmap, and $E000 to $C000), and clears the timer state.

Clears the timer state and rebuilds the plane at $E000 from the bitmap $2000-$3FFF, pixel by pixel from the top: every set pixel becomes the edge pattern if it is colour 3 (pixel_masks) and pattern_masks2 otherwise. Then sets $4E bit 7 and redraws the border.
Sets $D030 to 0 (a C128 at 1 MHz), waits for raster line 251, and turns all sprites off.

Loads the level's settings from the tables at $1181-$121A, indexed by the level $B7 (1 to 10; from 11 on it alternates 10 and 11): $1785, $6F, the timer-run limit $91D9, $91D5, $91D6, $91D7, $6E, $6D, the required claim $B8 (percent), $6C, $BB, $BE ($80 in practice), $159B and $15BE. The Qix colour $0205 is copied to $90EB, $15B7 and $15BB, its high nibble to $15B8 and $15BC. Then it clears the screen matrix's play area (35 columns of 24 rows from $0428) to colour 0, puts colour $22 in the panel column, draws the panel colours ($1D9C) and fills colour RAM from $D800 with 1 (fill_pages_from at $98F3).
Byte 2 of the LDA at $9089 in level_params (its operand), referred to by tune5_v1: an operand the code rewrites or reads as data.
The operand of the LDA at $90EA in level_params, rewritten at run time by level_params (self-modifying code).
Adds A (low) and X (high) to the level bonus at $028F/$0290.
Passes before the roamers start moving: 32 at the start of a round (level_start), 1 in the attract demo; enemies_step counts it down.

Resets the sprites for a round: no expansion, all hires, all off (wait_bottom_sprites_off), positions 0 and colour 1 (white); pointers $26 for sprite 1 and $22/$23 alternately for sprites 2-7; $15C9/$15CB/$15CD = $20 and $15CA/$15CC/$15CE = $40. Then marker_place.

Puts the marker at its position ($31,$32): copies it to the candidate ($0206,$0207), the last corner ($29,$2A), the plotter's two slots ($0C/$0E, $0D/$0F) and $ADEA/$ADEB, places the sprite (marker_sprite at $8CCA), runs $A1C0, and clears the drawing state ($9A, $9B, $6A, $6B, $9C), $1E, $5D, $027A, $AB, play_frozen ($15C8), $2B, the stick and count_8B08; $5F = 16, keep_bitmap ($1558) = $80.
Level setting from the table at $11CD, compared with var_9122's companion at $A1C2.
Level setting from the table at $11D8: the timer run at which timer_bar_empty speeds the pair at $92-$95 (and compared at $A23C).
Level setting from the table at $11E3, compared at $A318.
Bit 7 set when the Sparx timer has run out for the last time this life; the bar is no longer drawn or counted.
Level setting from the table at $11EE: how many times the timer bar may run out before it stops (timer_bar_empty).

Puts both Qix in the middle of the field. Sets the inner limits (qix_limits), the trail indices $B5/$B6/$AF/$B0 to $156B (the trail length less one), empties both trails (the eight ten-entry tables at $021E-$026D: x1, y1, x2, y2 for Qix 1, the same for Qix 2), and starts each Qix as the line from (centre x - 5, centre y - 5) to (centre x + 5, centre y + 5), held in $0287-$028E and the copies at $020C-$0213. The endpoint speeds come from random_speed ($A557, $A564): $C3/$C4 and $C7/$C8 for the first endpoint, $CB/$CC and $CF/$D0 for the second.
The box the Qix moves in: two pixels inside the field on every side, at $C2 (left), $C1 (right), $C0 (top), $BF (bottom).

Moves Qix 1's first endpoint vertically: y1 + speed $C7. Outside $C0-$BF the speed is reversed and re-randomised (negate_speed_y at $A555, plus the bias $0274 towards the marker) and the old position kept; a new countdown is drawn (new_turn_time). The result goes to $D4.
As qix1_move_y1 for Qix 1's first endpoint across the field: x1 + speed $C3, limits $C2-$C1, bias $0275, result in $D3.

Moves Qix 1's second endpoint vertically (speed $CF, bias $0274), then keeps it within the line-length limits of the first: while the distance between y2 and y1 is outside $156F-$1570 it is stepped by $156E towards range. Result in $D6.
As qix1_move_y2 for the horizontal coordinate (speed $CB, bias $0275, gap to $D3), result in $D5.
As qix1_move_y1 for Qix 2 (position $028D, bias $0276).
As qix1_move_y2 for Qix 2 (position $028E, bias $0276).
As qix1_move_x1 for Qix 2 (position $028B, bias $0277).
As qix1_move_x2 for Qix 2 (position $028C, bias $0277).
Cleared by qix_reset; nothing else uses it.

Moves a Qix one step. On levels with two Qix ($BB bit 7) it alternates between them ($027A bit 7; Qix 2 is qix2_step). For Qix 1: erases the oldest line of its trail (erase_segment), takes the current line and speeds, and counts down the turn time $0271; at zero a new random time is drawn (masked by the level's $6F), the hum (sound 3, or 4 for a long time) starts if it is not already playing, and each of the four speeds is re-randomised with probability 3/4. Then the four endpoints move (qix1_move_*), the colour and pattern are chosen ($98EB, $98C7), the new line is checked against the walls (qix1_check_line), stored as the newest entry of the trail and as the current line, and the bias towards the marker is chosen for each axis: $6E if the Qix is to the left of (or above) the marker, $6D otherwise.
qix_step for Qix 2: trail at $0246-$026D (index $B6), speeds at $027F-$0282, turn time $0272, moves qix2_move_*, wall check qix2_check_line, bias in $0276/$0277.

Tests Qix 1's new line against what is drawn: each of its sides is traced (line_test at $A62C, which sets $0285 bit 7 on a set pixel), and for each side that would cross a wall the endpoint's move is undone and re-randomised. If the line still crosses, the line falls back to the newest one in the trail and the turn time is cleared. The result becomes the current line, and is drawn (draw_qix_line).
Stores the line in $D3-$D6 as Qix 1's current line ($0287-$028A) and draws it (draw_qix_line).
qix1_check_line for Qix 2.
Stores the line in $D3-$D6 as Qix 2's current line ($028B-$028E) and draws it.
Draws the line from ($D3,$D4) to ($D5,$D6) with the line routine (line_start at $A5F4, in plot mode: $B3 = $80); entry $98A5 (BIT skip, $B3 = 0) erases it instead (erase_segment).
Erases the line ($D3,$D4)-($D5,$D6) by drawing it again in XOR mode ($B3 = 0).
Starts a line at X,Y with $0285 (the hit flag) cleared, in the mode $B3 chooses: line_start_plot ($A5F4) or line_start_test ($A5F6).
Chooses the Qix's pixel pattern for this step: $4F from qix_patterns by the random colour index $B1 (1 if it was 0), $50 = $AA.
The pixel patterns a Qix line can be drawn in: $00, $55, $AA, $FF (colours 0-3 of a multicolour byte).
Puts a random number in $0273: a value from $20 to $3E is kept, any other is cut to 0-3. Then falls into qix_colour.
A random number 0-3 into $B1, the index into qix_patterns.
Fills four pages (1 KB) from X,Y with A: used to fill colour RAM.
Fills $1F40 bytes (one bitmap) from X,Y (address high, low) with A.

One step of a line being drawn. $33 bit 7 toggles each call, and on alternate calls, while fire is held ($52 bit 4), the step is skipped unless $154D bit 7 or count_8B08 is set: a slow draw moves at half the speed of a fast one. Otherwise the marker advances twice (draw_advance): each new pixel goes in the plotter slots ($0C/$0E, then $0D/$0F). Reaching the edge ($28 bit 7) or failing to move ends the line: the last pixel is plotted (plot_line_pixel with $9B = $80), $5F is set to 8 if $155B bit 7 is set, and if the line ends with fire released ($27 bit 7 clear) and $154D clear, $23 is set to $80: the line counts as fast. Then the drawing flags are cleared.
The end of a drawn line: $9B from A, the last pixel plotted (plot_line_pixel), $5E set to 0 or $80 (BIT skip at $99AA) and the drawing flag $9A cleared.

Advances the marker one pixel in the held direction ($52: 8 right, 4 left, 1 up, 2 down, tried in that order and remembered in $9E), and sets up the three pixels to check: two beside the new position ($12/$15 and $13/$16) and one two pixels ahead ($14/$17). Then draw_check.

Checks the new pixel in the $E000 plane. Colour 3 (the edge): the line is complete ($28 = $80, $5E cleared) and the neighbours are checked as for empty ground. Colour 2: the marker is hit ($1E = $80; $28, $5E and $11 cleared). Colour 1: nothing more. Empty: the two side pixels and the pixel ahead are checked in turn; a colour-2 pixel among them is a hit, a colour-1 pixel ends the check, and if none of the three is colour 1, $11 is set to $80.

Plots the marker's pixel in colour 1 in all three planes: $E000 (the one the game tests), $6000 and the visible bitmap at $2000, unless the pixel there is already colour 3 (the marker is back on the edge), colour 1, or colour 2 (hit: $1E = $80). Then moves the marker sprite to it (marker_move).

Moves the two free-roaming creatures on sprites 2 and 3 (positions $90/$91 and $8E/$8F, directions $81/$82), used instead of the third pair of edge-walkers when the level's $BE allows. Each takes a new diagonal direction from roam_next_dir ($9D47), which looks at the walls round it, steps (diag_offset) and places its sprite (place_enemy_sprite). One with no way out ($9D47 returns 0) waits ($BD bit 7 or 6, counters $1556/$9C56 and $1557/$9C57) and then starts again from a Qix (spritz1_spawn, spritz2_spawn).
Steps X,Y one pixel diagonally by direction A: 1 right and up, 2 right and down, 4 left and down, 8 left and up; any other value leaves them.
Starts the first roamer at a Qix's midpoint (qix_midpoint, into $90/$91), sets $1559 = $80, and its direction to 1 (right and up).
Holds the first roamer back: sets $BD bit 7 and its two counters ($1556 and $9C56) to 3.
Starts the second roamer at a Qix's midpoint (into $8E/$8F), $1559 = $80, direction 4 (left and down).
Holds the second roamer back: sets $BD bit 6 and its counters ($1557 and $9C57) to 4.
Frame counter for the first roamer's wait.
Frame counter for the second roamer's wait.
Toggled by qix_midpoint: which Qix the next roamer starts from on two-Qix levels.
The middle of a Qix's current line, in X,Y: Qix 1's ($0210-$0213), or on levels with two Qix ($BB bit 7) Qix 2's ($020C-$020F) every other call.

Tests one of the twelve points round a roamer (offsets roam_dx/roam_dy, index X) in the $6000 plane and the $E000 plane. Touching colour 1 in the $6000 plane (the line being drawn) kills the marker ($1E = $80). A set pixel in the $E000 plane that is not colour 2 is a wall: its bit (roam_bits) is added to $9E3E. On levels where $9E3C bit 7 is set the probe is the version at $B684.

Chooses a roamer's next direction. Probes the twelve points round it (roam_probe) into a wall pattern; no walls: keep the direction in A. Otherwise the pattern is looked up in roam_patterns, and the matching entry of the table for the current direction (roam_turn_1, roam_turn_2, roam_turn_4 or roam_turn_8) is the new direction, 0 for none. A pattern of $FF (walls all round) sets $154D bit 7 and clears the hit flag: trapped.

The 28 wall patterns roam_next_dir recognises, as bits of the probe pattern: 12 single walls and corners, 12 pairs, and 4 more.

Places enemy sprite X/2 (X = 0 for sprite 2 up to 10 for sprite 7) at the pixel $88,$89: x = (x + 7) * 2 with the ninth bit in $D010, y = y + 40. If the position is either of the marker's plotter slots ($0C/$0E, $0D/$0F), the marker is hit ($1E = $80).

Moves the enemies once a pass of the main loop: walker pair B (walker_pair_b) except in practice; walker pair A (walker_pair_a) unless $BE bit 6 is set; walker pair C (walker_pair_c) unless $BE bit 7 is set; checking for a hit after each. With $BE bit 6 the second roamer pair (roam2_step, sprites 6-7) moves instead of pair A, and with bit 7 the first roamer pair (spritz_step, sprites 2-3) instead of pair C, both only once roamer_delay has counted down to 0 (one count a pass).

Walker pair A, sprites 6 and 7: only once the timer has run out at least lvl_91D5 times. Each walker waits out its start delay ($15C9, $15CA), then steps along the edge (walker_step_cw for one, walker_step_ccw for the other) and is placed; both are then shown in multicolour.

Walker pair B, sprites 4 and 5, which move every pass (walker_b1_step, walker_b2_step) and are shown each time. Once the timer has run out lvl_91D6 times their colours are set to 0, and on levels where $159B bit 7 is set they turn yellow (7) and begin to chase: a walker standing on the marker's last corner ($29,$2A) sets $6A or $6B, and from then on follows the marker's line (chaser_b1_step, chaser_b2_step). The code reads the colour back to alternate between 7 and 5, but it has just written 0 there, so the 5 is never chosen.

Walker pair B's first Sparx (sprite 5): chases up the line (chaser_b1_step) once it is on it ($6A bit 7); otherwise it resolves a meeting with its partner (walker_pair_b_sync), waits out its start delay ($15CB), steps along the edge (walker_step_cw) and is placed (place sprite at offset 6).
Walker pair B's second Sparx (sprite 4): chases up the line (chaser_b2_step) once on it ($6B bit 7); otherwise waits out its start delay ($15CC), steps along the edge (walker_step_ccw) and is placed.
Walker pair C, sprites 2 and 3: only once the timer has run out lvl_91D7 times; as walker_pair_a.

Carry set if the pixel at X,Y is colour 3, the edge.

The pixel one step to the walker's right, kept in $9F11/$9F12.
The pixel one step ahead, kept in $9F13/$9F14.

The direction from the walker's position ($88,$89) to X,Y.

Starts a line at X,Y in plot mode ($4E bit 7 set).

One step of line_to along the major axis.
The attract demo's version of round_intro: the burst plays with $74 set, then the sprites go off; no life is taken.

Opens a round: $74 = $80, panel redrawn, the converging-sprites animation (marker_burst at $A774) and sprites_off ($AB74); then, if a life was lost ($0202 bit 7), one life is taken from lives ($026E) and the panel redrawn. Entry $A704 only clears $0202.
Plays the recorded burst back, one frame per call from the end ($73 counting down): for each frame the four sprite pointers and positions come from the tables at $6000-$6C00 that marker_burst filled.

The marker's burst: four sprites start at the marker ($75-$7C all at $31,$32), pointers $30 and $38, and move out diagonally one pixel a frame towards the four corners of the field ($1579-$157C) until they reach them (burst_frame); each frame is recorded at $6000-$6C00. With $74 bit 7 set (a round starting) the recording is played backwards (burst_replay), so the sprites converge on the marker instead.

One frame of marker_burst: steps each of the four sprites one pixel diagonally until it reaches its corner limit, places them (burst_place_1/2/4/8), records the frame, and repeats while any is still moving.
Places burst sprite 1 (A = 1; entries $A88F, $A892, $A895 with the BIT skip give 2, 4 and 8) at X,Y unless it is on a corner limit: x doubled into $D000+ (table $1585), ninth bit in $D010.

Entry of burst_place_1 for sprite 4 (A = 4, BIT skip).

Before a fill, finds which side of the new line the Qix is on: from Qix 1's centre point ($0210,$0211) it walks right to the first edge pixel, remembers that pixel ($0208,$0209), and then follows the edge round (fill_follow_*) until it comes back to it. Ends the edge walk when it is back at its start (fill_at_start).

Draws a line from the start to X,Y with Bresenham's method through plot_all.

Turns sprites 0-3 off, freezes play ($15C8 = $80), and resets all eight sprites to position 0, colour 1, no expansion.

One frame of music, from the interrupt.
